A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multimodal token-compression survey. All 20 pages of v4 and 42 pages of v5 are readable, including equations, figures, tables, references, and v4's author biographies. Neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: v4 reviews published methods and their reported results, including Tables II–III. It reports no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or empirical data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v5 remains a literature survey. Figure 4 explicitly uses configurations and results reported by the cited methods; Table 4 catalogs benchmarks. Neither establishes original empirical results produced by this work.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an original compression algorithm or model. v5's new definition and descriptions of additional published techniques change the survey's documentation and scope discussion, not a proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The retained result tables cover the same benchmarks. Additional benchmarks in Table 4, including PerceptionTest and temporal grounding, are described or recommended without new training or evaluation on them.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables II/2 and III/3 is unchanged. Figure 4 compiles additional literature curves, but neither version evaluates comparison methods against an original proposed method.

E3.justification: Model labels, resolutions, token counts, retention ratios, and metric columns remain unchanged in the matched tables. Table 4 supplies benchmark guidance without establishing a revised protocol for those results or newly conducted evaluations.

E4.justification: No new ablation, robustness test, sensitivity experiment, error analysis, or case study is reported. Figure 4 visualizes published operating points; the expanded discussions provide conceptual synthesis rather than additional experimental analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the comparisons. Figure 4 introduces no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables II–III are numerically retained as Tables 2–3, but Figure 4 adds literature performance-versus-retention points, including PDrop and VidCom2. Some values are unreconciled with the tables: ToMe appears near 63 at approximately 33% retention, versus 68.0 for 192/576 tokens in the retained image table. The configuration caveat prevents interpreting this as a demonstrated same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: New Section 2.4 formally defines a compression operator mapping N tokens to M tokens with M < N, distinguishes input-level from feature-level compression, and excludes attention sparsity that preserves sequence length. The existing equations remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contribution: a structured survey organized by image, video, and audio modalities and four compression mechanisms. The new title and rewritten conclusion do not introduce a different core contribution.

C2.justification: v4 Section VI-C broadly argues that combining compression methods often fails. v5 Section 6.3 replaces this with differentiated explanations of orthogonal combinations, complementary hybrids such as VisionZip, and conflicting filters. Sections 5.5, 6.4, and 6.7 also substantially extend interpretations of audio redundancy, useful contextual noise, cross-modal compression, and future architectural directions.

D1.justification: Table 4 adds practical documentation of benchmark task types, metrics, and system prompts. Conversely, v5 removes v4's access link to the maintained token-compression repository. These are documentation changes, not evidence of changed experimental execution.

R1.justification: v5 substantially expands connections to KV-cache compression, sparse and linear attention, recent audio compression, and omnimodal systems, including H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, and OmniZip. It also adds benchmark references and removes the MoB citation accompanying v4's earlier argument against combining compression methods.

P1.justification: The survey is retitled, selected passages and the conclusion are rewritten, and focused subsections and acknowledgments are added. Author biographies are removed and citations become author–year. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The two-column format is replaced by a single-column TMLR layout throughout. Figures and tables are resized and relocated, Figure 1's panels become side by side, and the taxonomy occupies a full page. Figure 4 and Table 4 are added, while biography portraits disappear.

improvement.justification: v5 improves scope clarity and replaces v4's broad warning about combining methods with a more informative discussion. However, its new Figure 4 introduces numerical differences from the retained tables, such as ToMe near 63 versus 68.0, without enough configuration detail to reconcile them. The repository pointer also disappears. These gains in synthesis coexist with reduced quantitative clarity and resource discoverability, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
